selected_option: YAML as an explicitly applied editable source representation and interchange format over the canonical DesignDocument
selection_reason: It gives people and agents a lower-punctuation authoring surface while retaining the existing validated object model, optimistic revisions, and rendering pipeline. Canonical-YAML storage creates disproportionate migration and compatibility risk; import/export alone omits useful in-product validation and preview feedback.

alternatives.title: YAML as editable source representation
alternatives.user_value: High: inspect or edit the complete design as text, validate it, preview changes, and explicitly apply them.
alternatives.complexity: Medium: shared codec, source editor, diagnostics, CLI format support, documentation, and cross-client capability discovery.
alternatives.compatibility: High when YAML converts into the unchanged DesignDocument and saves through existing services.
alternatives.round_trip: Semantic DesignDocument equality; lexical formatting and comments are not preserved after apply.
alternatives.data_loss_risk: Low for supported document data after schema validation; comments, anchors, aliases, tags, and author formatting are intentionally outside persistence.
alternatives.schema_evolution: Uses existing schemaVersion and upgrade rules; YAML adds no independent product schema.
alternatives.validation_ux: Strong: parse diagnostics plus existing Zod paths before preview/apply.
alternatives.ai_usability: High: agents may emit a readable full document but still face deterministic validation and revision checks.
alternatives.maintenance_burden: Moderate and bounded by a single shared codec.

alternatives.title: YAML import/export only
alternatives.user_value: Medium: useful external interchange, but validation and correction are displaced outside the editor.
alternatives.compatibility: High with shared conversion to DesignDocument.
alternatives.data_loss_risk: Low with strict validation; comments still disappear on re-export.
alternatives.validation_ux: Weaker: import is a one-shot failure loop.
alternatives.ai_usability: Good for file workflows, weaker for interactive repair.

alternatives.title: YAML as canonical source of truth
alternatives.user_value: No clear incremental user value over an alternate source view.
alternatives.complexity: Very high: database migration, API contract change, publication/history compatibility, and parser semantics become persistence semantics.
alternatives.compatibility: Poor without broad migration and dual-format support.
alternatives.round_trip: Would require lexical-source persistence or comment loss despite calling YAML canonical.
alternatives.data_loss_risk: High during migration and across old clients.
alternatives.schema_evolution: Duplicates existing schemaVersion concerns with format migration.
alternatives.validation_ux: Potentially strong but not unique to canonical storage.
alternatives.ai_usability: High authorability but little advantage over alternate representation.

alternatives.title: Generated/read-only YAML
alternatives.user_value: Low: easier inspection but no direct correction workflow.
alternatives.round_trip: Not applicable because edits cannot return.

alternatives.title: Improve the visual editor without YAML
alternatives.user_value: High for visual workflows but does not address complete-document text authoring or agent-readable interchange.
alternatives.ai_usability: Does not materially improve text authoring.

alternatives.title: Defer or do not build YAML
alternatives.user_value: Avoids new dependency and surface area but leaves a credible human/agent authoring need unmet.
